# The documented command line of the data-validation program, release 8.9.3,
# written from its README and `--help` pages (the program is not installed
# where these tests run). A `feature:` line is a command or a documented
# call; any other line that starts with a dash is an option, its aliases
# first. The test holds migkit's account of the program to this file.
feature: validate column :: compare aggregates of columns between two tables
  --count COLUMNS             count of non-null values of the columns
  --sum COLUMNS               sum of the columns
  --min COLUMNS               smallest value of the columns
  --max COLUMNS               largest value of the columns
  --avg COLUMNS               mean of the columns
  --std COLUMNS               standard deviation of the columns
  --bit_xor COLUMNS           bitwise xor over the columns
  -gc, --grouped-columns COLS aggregate per distinct value of these columns
  -ec, --exclude-columns      take every column except the ones listed
  -th, --threshold FLOAT      percent of difference tolerated before a fail
  -filters, --filters TEXT    a WHERE clause on source and target
  -wis, --wildcard-include-string-len  include string columns when columns are wildcarded
  -wit, --wildcard-include-timestamp   include timestamp columns when columns are wildcarded
  -ctb, --cast-to-bigint      cast integer columns to bigint before a sum
feature: validate row :: compare rows by hash or by the compared fields
  --hash COLUMNS              compare a hash of the columns of each row
  --concat COLUMNS            compare the concatenated columns of each row
  -comp-fields, --comparison-fields COLS  columns whose values are compared
  -pk, --primary-keys COLS    columns that line the rows up
  -rr, --use-random-row       compare a random sample of rows
  -rbs, --random-row-batch-size INT  how many rows the sample takes
  -cim, --case-insensitive-match     ignore case when matching keys
  -mcc, --max-concat-columns INT     most columns concatenated at once
  -tsp, --trim-string-pks     trim whitespace from string keys
  --trim-whitespace           trim whitespace from every string column
feature: validate schema :: compare column names and types of two tables
  -ec, --exclusion-columns COLS  columns left out of the schema comparison
  -al, --allow-list TEXT         type mappings accepted as equal
  -alf, --allow-list-file PATH   file of type mappings accepted as equal
feature: validate custom-query column :: aggregates over the result of a query
feature: validate custom-query row :: rows of the result of a query
  -sq, --source-query TEXT       query run on the source
  -tq, --target-query TEXT       query run on the target
  -sqf, --source-query-file PATH query file run on the source
  -tqf, --target-query-file PATH query file run on the target
  -rh, --result-handler TEXT     where results are stored
  -bqrh, --bq-result-handler TEXT  older name of the result handler
  -sa, --service-account PATH    cloud account for the result handler
  -l, --labels TEXT              labels attached to every result
  -c, --config-file PATH         write the validation to a YAML file
feature: configs run :: run validations stored in YAML files
feature: configs list :: list the stored validations
feature: configs get :: print one stored validation
  -cj, --config-file-json PATH   stored validation in JSON
  -cdir, --config-dir PATH       directory of stored validations
  -cdj, --config-dir-json PATH   directory of stored JSON validations
  -kc, --kube-completions        run indexed jobs for a directory of validations
  -fmt, --format TEXT            how results are printed
  -fs, --filter-status TEXT      keep only results of this status
  --run-id TEXT                  identifier of the run
  -dr, --dry-run                 print the validation instead of running it
  -v, --verbose                  verbose logging
  -ll, --log-level TEXT          log level
feature: generate-table-partitions :: split a table into key ranges as stored validations
  -pn, --partition-num INT       how many partitions
  -ppf, --parts-per-file INT     partitions written to one file
feature: find-tables :: pair the tables of two schemas by name
  -as, --allowed-schemas TEXT    schemas searched
  -iv, --include-views           pair views as well
  --score-cutoff FLOAT  least name similarity accepted
  -q, --query TEXT               the query
  --conn TEXT           connection the query runs on
  -sc, --source-conn TEXT        connection of the source
  -tc, --target-conn TEXT        connection of the target
  -tbls, --tables-list TEXT      tables compared, source=target pairs
feature: connections add :: store a connection
  -c, --connection-name TEXT     name the connection is stored under
feature: connections list :: list stored connections
feature: connections delete :: remove a stored connection
feature: connections describe :: show one stored connection
  -sm, --secret-manager-type TEXT        secret manager holding the credentials
  -sp, --secret-manager-project-id TEXT  project of the secret manager
